title: 1. HoneyChain App Structure
content:
- **Home**: Overview of apiary statistics (total hives, active colonies, total harvested honey, latest telemetry weight trends, and quick action shortcuts).
- **My Apiary**: Unified workspace for registered hives, recording honey harvests, tracking historical scale measurements, and managing honey traceability batches.
- **Schemes**: Official government apiculture subsidies, mission grants, documentation checklists, and application guidelines.
- **Profile**: Beekeeper profile settings, apiary name, jurisdiction/district details, multilingual preferences (Kannada, Hindi, English), and sign out.

title: 2. Talk to HoneyChain Voice Support
content:
- Tap the floating green microphone icon at the bottom right corner of the screen.
- Select your preferred language: **Kannada (ಕನ್ನಡ)**, **Hindi (हिन्दी)**, or **English**.
- **Push-to-Talk**: Press and hold the microphone button to speak your question in natural language.
- Release the button to send. The assistant transcribes your audio, checks your actual registered hive telemetry, retrieves scientific knowledge, and speaks the answer back.
- **Barge-In**: If the assistant is speaking and you need to ask another question, simply press the mic button again; audio playback stops immediately.
- If you need human assistance, tap **Request Human Callback** to create an official support request for a district apiculture agent.

title: 1. Safety and Advisory Disclaimer
content: - *Notice*: HoneyChain provides advisory educational guidance only. Never apply unverified chemicals or pesticides. Always consult an authorized district apicultural officer or university agricultural extension specialist (KVK) for disease confirmation and regulated treatments.

title: 2. Common Colony Warning Signs
content:
- **Varroa Mites (*Varroa destructor*)**:
  - Small reddish-brown parasites visible on adult bees and capped drone brood.
  - Deformed wing virus (stunted wings on newly emerged bees).
  - High mite infestation causes colony collapse. Use sticky boards on bottom boards to monitor daily mite drop count.
- **American Foulbrood (AFB)**:
  - Sunken, dark, perforated brood cappings with a sulfurous foul odor.
  - Matchstick test: Insert a matchstick into an affected cell; if ropey mucus draws out > 2 cm, AFB is suspected.
  - Highly contagious bacterial spore; immediately notify local agricultural authorities. Quarantine affected equipment.
- **European Foulbrood (EFB)**:
  - Larvae die before capping, turning yellow-brown and twisting into unnatural 'C' shapes at cell bottoms.
- **Wax Moth Infestation**:
  - Silken webs, tunnels, and powdery frass through comb frames, typically attacking weak or abandoned colonies.
  - Prevent by keeping strong colonies, reducing empty supers, and trapping adult moths.

title: 3. General Health Best Practices
content:
- Keep colonies strong with young, prolific queens.
- Sterilize hive tools with alcohol or torch flame between inspecting different apiaries.
- Avoid transferring frames from sickly hives to healthy hives.

title: 1. National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)
content:
- **Ministry**: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India (Sweet Revolution).
- **Core Objectives**: Promoting scientific beekeeping, setting up custom hiring centers, disease diagnostic labs, and honey testing labs.
- **Components**:
  - Mini Mission I: Production & productivity enhancement (subsidies on bee boxes, bee colonies, and honey extractors up to 40% to 50% for individual farmers and higher for SC/ST/Women/FPOs).
  - Mini Mission II: Post-harvest management, collection centers, cold storage, and traceability systems.
  - Mini Mission III: Research, apicultural education, and skill development.

title: 2. KVIC Honey Mission
content:
- **Agency**: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of MSME.
- Distribution of modern bee boxes with live bee colonies (*Apis cerana indica*) to traditional pot-hive beekeepers and rural youth along with training toolkits.

title: 3. State Apiculture Initiatives (e.g. Karnataka Horticulture)
content:
- Schemes supported by Department of Horticulture (Government of Karnataka) provide 50% capital subsidy on bee colonies, Langstroth boxes, extractors, and smoker kits.
- Verification and applications can be processed through local Senior Assistant Directors of Horticulture (SADH) or Raitha Samparka Kendras (RSK).

title: 4. Viewing Schemes in HoneyChain
content:
- Tap the **Schemes** bottom navigation tab in HoneyChain.
- View verified national and state schemes, eligibility requirements, required identity documents (Aadhaar, Land RTC / Survey, Bank Passbook), and direct official portal links.
- Tap the bookmark icon to save schemes for quick access.

title: 1. Registering a New Colony
content:
- In HoneyChain, each hive represents a physical apicultural colony (Langstroth, Newton, or traditional box).
- To register a hive: Navigate to the **My Apiary** tab, tap **Add Hive**, enter the hive name (e.g., "North Orchard Box 1"), installation location, frame count (standard 8 or 10 frames), and initial health status.
- Once registered, a unique Hive ID is generated (e.g., `HIVE-XXXX`).

title: 2. Colony Inspections and Routine Checks
content:
- Weekly brood inspections should check for queen laying patterns, drone cells, stored pollen, and honey reserves.
- Look for uniform brood patterns. Spotty brood can indicate queen failure or nutritional stress.
- Frame counts: Ensure space is added (super boxes) before 80% of current frames are capped to prevent swarming.

title: 3. Apiary Placement Guidelines
content:
- Hives should face East or South-East to catch morning sunlight, encouraging early foraging.
- Provide windbreaks against strong seasonal drafts and ensure hives are elevated at least 30 cm off the ground to prevent dampness and predator (ant/termite) ingress.
- Ensure accessible fresh water within 500 meters of the apiary.

title: 4. Seasonal Adjustments
content:
- **Monsoon / Rainy Season**: Elevate hive entrances, ensure hive roofs are waterproof, and provide sugar syrup or pollen patties if natural foraging drops significantly.
- **Summer / Heatwaves**: Provide shade covers or canvas damp cloths over supers. Adequate ventilation is required to prevent comb melting.
- **Winter**: Reduce entrance size to retain hive heat and prevent robbing.

title: 1. When to Harvest Honey
content:
- Harvest only fully capped honey frames (at least 75% to 80% capped with wax). Uncapped nectar has high moisture (> 20%) and will ferment into mead or spoil rapidly.
- Standard honey moisture should ideally be below 19% (FSSAI apicultural standard is ≤ 20%).
- Harvest during dry, warm mid-day hours when foragers are out in the field.

title: 2. Extraction Best Practices
content:
- Never use direct heat or boiling water on raw honey. Excessive heat (> 40°C) destroys beneficial bee enzymes (diastase, invertase) and increases HMF (Hydroxymethylfurfural) levels.
- Use a stainless steel hand or motorized centrifugal extractor.
- Filter through food-grade double mesh (coarse 18 mesh followed by fine 100 mesh) to remove wax particles while preserving microscopic pollen grains.

title: 3. Recording a Harvest in HoneyChain
content:
- Open **My Apiary** or tap **Record Harvest** on the Home screen.
- Select the specific source hive(s) from which the honey was extracted.
- Enter net extracted weight in kilograms (kg), date of extraction, honey floral source (e.g., Multifloral, Acacia, Jamun, Mustard, Wild Forest), and optional moisture percentage.
- Tapping **Save Harvest** automatically generates a traceable **Honey Batch** linked to those exact colonies.

title: 1. Traceability Principle
content:
- In HoneyChain, raw honey must never appear out of nowhere. Every consumer batch is cryptographically tied to verified source colonies and real beekeeper registrations.
- Traceability data includes: Apiary location, Extraction date, Floral classification, Source Hive IDs, Moisture %, Beekeeper identification, and Public verification status.

title: 2. Batch Creation Lifecycle
content:
- When a harvest is recorded in HoneyChain, a batch code with prefix `HC-` (e.g., `HC-2026-B001`) is minted.
- The batch is stored privately under the beekeeper's account and synchronized to the public verification registry `public_batches/{batchCode}`.
- The public record contains immutable verification data viewable by consumers without needing login.

title: 3. Combating Adulteration
content:
- Traditional honey in commercial markets is frequently adulterated with C4/C3 inverted sugar syrups, rice syrup, or high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS).
- HoneyChain ensures origin integrity by linking harvest volume directly to hive scale weight drops and registered colony capacities.

title: 1. Jar QR Codes
content:
- Every recorded Honey Batch has a distinct verification QR code generated inside HoneyChain.
- Beekeepers can view and print this QR code by going to **My Apiary** ➔ **Honey Traceability** ➔ **Generate / View QR**.
- The QR contains a universal URL: `https://honeychain.app/verify/<BATCH_CODE>` (or deep link `honeychain://verify/<BATCH_CODE>`).

title: 2. Public Consumer Verification (Zero Login Required)
content:
- Consumers do not need an account, app installation, or login to verify a jar.
- Any smartphone camera or browser can open the verification link, displaying:
  - Official HoneyChain Authenticity Seal.
  - Apiary Name & State/District of origin.
  - Harvest date and net quantity.
  - Floral honey classification (e.g. Pure Multifloral Raw Honey).
  - Registry Ready status confirmed against Firestore.

title: 3. In-App QR Scanner
content:
- Inside the HoneyChain app, beekeepers and customers can tap the camera QR icon in the top header to scan a physical jar QR directly.
- The scanner parses the batch code and pops up the live verification modal immediately.

title: 1. Supported Telemetry Hardware
content:
- **Microcontroller**: ESP32 with WiFi / Bluetooth LE / GSM SIM800L module.
- **Scale Subsystem**: 4x 50kg load cells in wheatstone bridge configuration (or single 200kg bar cell) with an **HX711** 24-bit ADC amplifier.
- **Climate Sensors**: DHT22 or SHT31 for internal hive temperature and relative humidity.

title: 2. Sensor Status Indicators in HoneyChain
content:
- **Live / Connected (Green)**: Fresh sensor readings received within the last 24 hours.
- **Stale (Amber)**: The last reading is older than 24 hours. Check ESP32 solar battery level or network connectivity.
- **Disconnected (Red)**: Device configured but no packet received for over 48 hours.
- **No Sensor**: The hive does not have a linked IoT device. Manual scale readings can be recorded anytime by tapping the hive in **My Apiary**.

title: 3. Weight Trend vs Honey Production
content:
- **Important**: Hive weight changes represent total colony mass fluctuations (brood growth, pollen reserves, nectar flow, water carrying, adult bee population, and wooden moisture).
- An increase in weight indicates net biomass/store gain, but is not 100% extracted honey until harvested.
- A sudden drop in hive weight of 1.5 kg to 3 kg in spring/summer frequently signals a **swarm event** (queen departed with half the colony). Check the apiary trees immediately.
- A steady daily weight decline in winter or dearth periods indicates colonies are consuming winter stores; emergency supplemental feeding may be required.

title: 4. Troubleshooting Steps for HX711 Scale
content:
- If readings fluctuate wildly: Check for moisture condensation on HX711 analog lines, ensure load cells have rigid corner shims, and check ground wires.
- If readings read constant zero: Verify clock (SCK) and data (DT) pin assignments on ESP32 GPIOs.
